newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MARINERS' RANDY JOHNSON MISSES START DUE TO SICK SON.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MARINERS' RANDY JOHNSON MISSES START DUE TO SICK SON.

text.p: The expected return of Seattle Mariners ace Randy Johnson was put on hold as he missed his scheduled start Friday night against the Boston Red Sox due to the hospitalization of his infant son.

Johnson's son Tanner, who turns one year old Saturday, was admitted to a local hospital Thursday afternoon due to a viral respiratory infection and stayed overnight as a precaution. He is expected to be released on Saturday.

Johnson will not be in uniform Friday and Bob Wolcott will take his place on the mound. Johnson, the 1995 American League Cy Young winner, is tentatively scheduled to start on Saturday in the middle game of the three-game series with Boston.

The 33-year-old Johnson was bothered by back trouble throughout the 1996 season. He was 5-0 with a 3.83 ERA in eight starts before going on the disabled list May 12. He was activated in August and was used primarily in relief before manager Lou Piniella decided to shut down his season.

Johnson's health is a key element in the Mariners' hopes of reaching their first World Series. He headlines a starting rotation that has been beefed up through the acquisition of National Leaguers Jeff Fassero and Scott Sanders.
The Mariners are 38-2 in Johnson's last 40 starts dating to July 31, 1994.

Johnson was 18-2 with a league-leading 2.48 ERA in 1995. The lanky lefthander also led the league in strikeouts for the fourth straight year with 294 and was 2-0 with a 2.70 ERA in the AL divisional playoffs against the New York Yankees.
Johnson has a career record of 104-60 in seven-plus major league seasons with Montreal and Seattle.
